item.title: Environmental Assessment of Wood Utilization
item.description:
Environmental Assessment of Wood Utilization

Assessing the environmental performance of wood products across their life cycle.

Overview
#

Wood utilization can contribute to climate change mitigation through carbon storage, material substitution, and the sustainable use of forest resources.

However, its environmental performance depends on multiple stages, including forest management, harvesting, transportation, processing, use, reuse, and disposal.

item.title: Regional Economic Impacts of Local Timber
item.description:
Regional Economic Impacts of Local Timber

Evaluating how forest resources contribute to regional industries and economic circulation.

Overview
#

Forestry and wood utilization generate economic activity through forest management, harvesting, transportation, processing, construction, energy use, and related services.

The economic effects of these activities extend beyond the forestry sector itself.

This project evaluates how the production and use of local timber contribute to employment, income, industrial activity, and regional economic circulation.

item.title: People, Biodiversity, and Satoyama
item.description:
People, Biodiversity, and Satoyama

Exploring relationships between forest ecosystems, local communities, and human activities.

Overview
#

Satoyama forests have been shaped through long-term interactions between people and forest ecosystems.

Changes in forest use, management practices, population, and local economies can influence biodiversity, resource availability, and community relationships with forests.

This project examines the ecological and social dimensions of satoyama management.
